kill_fact: The adverse case's fiscal-2027 revenue of $1.20 billion is below the backlog the company has already disclosed as convertible inside twelve months. On the 4 August 2026 call the chief financial officer gave the figure directly: of the $2.4 billion backlog, just under $1.3 billion converts over the next twelve months (about 54%), plus roughly $75 million a quarter of book-and-bill work that never enters backlog. The adverse case's own text says the existing backlog still converts, so $1.20 billion is internally inconsistent with its own premise -- it requires Powell to fail to deliver contracted work in the same year it adds over 20% to its manufacturing footprint. The prior-year analogue makes the point arithmetically: a year earlier about 62% of a $1.433 billion book, roughly $0.89 billion, was called convertible, and the company then billed $1.157 billion in the twelve months to 30 June 2026 -- a 1.30 times realisation. The same 1.15 to 1.30 times realisation on $1.3 billion is $1.50 billion to $1.69 billion, not $1.20 billion. This does not break the thesis that the shares are unattractive -- concentration, project lumpiness and the fiscal-2021 near-zero trough all survive attack -- but it breaks the levels the thesis is priced off.
corrections: Four load-bearing items failed verification against the 3-4 August 2026 primary disclosures the record itself cites as its source. (1) BACKLOG TRUTH -- verifies exactly, no correction: record new orders $934 million, book-to-bill 3.0 times, backlog $2.4 billion (up $967 million year over year, $619 million sequentially), the three named mega awards (>$400 million behind-the-meter data centre Phase 1, ~$75 million petrochemical/fertiliser, ~$60 million liquefied natural gas) plus over $350 million of other awards, all confirmed verbatim on the 4 August 2026 call. What the record MISSED from that same call is the conversion disclosure -- $1.3 billion convertible in twelve months, 54%, down from the low 60s -- which the record's forcing_function says must wait for the November annual report. It is already public, and it floors revenue above the adverse case. (2) GM-TRAJECTORY TRUTH -- the two quarters of year-over-year compression verify from the filed statements (30.57% versus 30.71% in the June quarter; 29.65% versus 29.94% in the March quarter), but the framing is cherry-picked to the quarter. On the nine months of fiscal 2026 gross margin is 29.63% against 28.63% a year earlier, up 100 basis points. And the closeout drag is materially overstated: the record uses 150 to 170 basis points and derives an as-sold margin 'nearer 28.5%'; the chief financial officer disclosed on 4 August 2026 that closeouts contributed roughly 100 basis points over the first nine months, against about 130 basis points a year ago. The closeout benefit is FALLING, so the underlying as-sold margin is improving, not deteriorating -- the opposite direction to the one the record trades on. (3) The claim that 'management now guides margin flat at the trailing-twelve-month level of about 30.1%' and 'has told the market not to expect improvement' is NOT in the primary source. Asked directly on 4 August 2026 whether margins had peaked, the chief executive said he would not say they had, and named automation and services as accretive to current gross margin. On pricing the record leans on an August 2025 quote ('the pricing is not improving') presented as current; twelve months later the same executive said Powell is seeing some opportunity for price in the market, with more of it on the commercial side. A stale quote is doing the work of a current one. (4) HIDDEN DISQUALIFIER, partly reversed: the record's execution leg -- 'a $2.4 billion backlog with no factory to run it through', 'the greenfield decision deferred again' -- is superseded. During the June quarter the Board authorised acquisition of a leased facility supporting approximately 300,000 square feet, targeted productive late in the second or early in the third quarter of fiscal 2027; Jacintoport's 335,000 square feet completes within one to two months; a 50,000 square foot Houston lease was signed in April and a 30,000 square foot Ohio lease carries an expansion option. Total footprint expands over 20% by the end of fiscal 2026. The record's own falsification test ('the greenfield decision deferred again') resolved against it. (5) The balance-sheet overlay rests on an unverified figure: 'customer advances rose about $263 million in the June quarter alone.' Filed contract liabilities went from $314.506 million at 31 March 2026 to $466.362 million at 30 June 2026 -- an increase of $151.9 million, overstating the float build by about $111 million and understating genuinely surplus cash by the same amount. What SURVIVES the attack and is not corrected: counterparty concentration is real and correctly sized (one undisclosed customer at roughly a sixth of backlog, later phases explicitly uncontracted -- the chief executive confirmed future phases only 'assuming we're successful'); petrochemical revenue down 49% verifies; insider behaviour verifies (no open-market purchases in the window -- the 1 July 2026 acquisition by the chief executive was a $0.01 option exercise, not a purchase); the 52-week low is $78.50, not the $69 the record cites; and the multiple critique stands. Price drift is immaterial ($208.79 on 11 August 2026 versus the $211.06 recorded).

corrections_typed.basis: Carried through from two verified input errors on the record's own schedule, multiple held unchanged at its blended 23.8 times: (i) fiscal-2027 revenue raised $1.38bn to $1.50bn, a conservative 1.15 times realisation on the $1.3bn of backlog management disclosed as twelve-month-convertible on 4 Aug 2026 versus the 1.30 times Powell actually delivered in the twelve months to 30 Jun 2026, and still below the ~$1.6bn implied by adding ~$75m/quarter of book-and-bill; (ii) EBITDA margin 20.0% to 20.5%, because the record's 150-170bp closeout drag is contradicted by the CFO's 100bp-of-nine-months figure (down from 130bp) on 4 Aug 2026, and trailing realised EBITDA margin is 21.5% ($248.98m on $1,157.52m, quarterly filings through 30 Jun 2026); (iii) net cash credited $300m to $400m, restoring the $111m by which the '$263m of customer advances' claim overstated the filed contract-liability build of $151.9m ($314.506m at 31 Mar 2026 to $466.362m at 30 Jun 2026). $1.50bn x 20.5% = $307.5m EBITDA x 23.8 = $7,318m + $400m = $7,718m / 36.566m diluted shares = $211.

Adverse-case revenue raised $1.20bn to $1.30bn, the exact figure the CFO disclosed on 4 Aug 2026 as convertible from existing backlog within twelve months (just under $1.3bn, ~54% of $2.4bn) -- crediting zero new orders and zero book-and-bill, so still genuinely adverse; the record's own 17% EBITDA margin, its own implied blended 15.9 times ($3.24bn operating EV on $204m) and its own $225m net-cash credit are all left untouched. $1.30bn x 17% = $221m x 15.9 = $3,514m + $225m = $3,739m / 36.566m diluted shares = $102. Note the record's own bear arithmetic also mis-sums: its six segment EVs of $3.24bn plus $225m over 36.57m shares is $94.7, not the $96 printed.
